what: Keystroke-Level Model operator times used to predict expert, error-free task times (benchmark_tasks.json). Read by generate_refs.mjs.
source: S1 Kieras 1993 tutorial (primary, downloaded, sha256 57e0bcde…1c02); S2 Wikipedia KLM table (secondary) agrees on K, P, B, H; S3 Card, Moran & Newell 1980 is the original (not read: paywalled). Grade A for K, P, B, BB, H (two independent sources agree); M differs between sources (1.2 s Kieras vs 1.35 s CMN as quoted by S2), so it is run at both values.

K.meaning: one keystroke (each key, Shift and Ctrl count separately)
K.quote: K - Keystroke (.12 - 1.2 sec; .28 recommended for most users)

P.meaning: point the mouse at a target (Fitts average)
P.quote: P - Point with mouse to a target on the display (1.1 sec)

B.meaning: press OR release a mouse button (drag = P B P B)
B.quote: B - Press or release mouse button (.1 sec)

H.meaning: home the hand between mouse and keyboard
H.quote: H - Home hands to keyboard or mouse (.4 sec)

M.quote: M - Mental act of routine thinking or perception (.6 - 1.35 sec; use 1.2 sec)

sensitivity.name: cmn-mental
sensitivity.why: S2 quotes the CMN M operator as 1.35 s

accuracy.source: S2 (secondary, grade B): 'has a root-mean-square error of 21%'

notation.K:<text>: one K per character; ⏎ Enter, ⇥ Tab, ␣ Space, ⇧ Shift, ^ Ctrl, ⎋ Esc, → arrow; {F8} is one key
notation.x<n>: a step suffix '*n' repeats the step n times, e.g. 'K:→*5'

placementRules: R1 one M before each command start (recall the alias / find the tool)
R2 one M before each typed value (recall it from the task sheet)
R3 one M before each pick that needs a visual search (find the snap / the object); a pick that only gives a direction (ortho / polar) has no M

R4 two-handed posture: left hand on the keyboard, right hand on the mouse; aliases, Enter, Space, Esc, Shift, Ctrl and F-keys need no H; numbers and arrows need the right hand: H before them and H before the next pointing
R5 the same rules for every design (S1: 'Consistency in M placement is more important than absolute accuracy')
